notes: §1985:XIV.3.6.3 SR2: "Identifier-2 must reference a one-character integer without an operational sign." CommunicationBinder#BindSend refuses (COBOL6171) any operand IsIntegerItem rejects or whose PicInfo is not Digits 1 unsigned; probes at --std 85 accept PIC 9, 9P, 9 COMP, a subscripted and a qualified PIC 9, and refuse P9, S9, S9 SIGN SEPARATE, 99, X, A, Z, 9 BLANK WHEN ZERO, 9V9, a group, a USAGE INDEX item, an index-name, I99(2:1), FUNCTION INTEGER/CHAR, ZERO (classes b, d). Two operand shapes under-reject: a reference-modified PIC 9 (I9 (1:1)) is accepted, though a reference-modified numeric item is class and category alphanumeric (§1985:IV.4.3.8.4.4 GR5), because IsIntegerItem reads the base item's PicInfo through the RefModPlace; and LINAGE-COUNTER of a LINAGE IS 60 file is accepted although its implicit description is an unsigned integer of the size of integer-1, two digits (§1985:VII.1.3.7), because IsIntegerItem answers true for every BoundComputedOperand without applying the one-digit test. No kb/Work note holds either (PB5289 landed the 9P/index/symbolic-character arms; PB5343 is the 2002-wording diagnostic). kb/Work PB5384 holds the defect (code read: coderead-85/out-reread2/rr-07.json).

next.reason: 1985: "Identifier-2 must reference a one-character integer without an operational sign."; 2023: "2023 SEND is the message-server SEND (message-server-name-1, message-tag data items); it has no end-indicator identifier-2.". The communication module's SEND and its end-indicator identifier-2 are gone. The 2023 SEND rules cover message servers only, and no candidate restates the one-character unsigned integer rule.
